design.quote: In this individual participant data (IPD) meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials

effect.quote: adjusted odds ratio 0.88, 95% confidence interval 0.81 to 0.96

duration.quote: participants were followed for a median of 12 months

funding.quote: This study was supported by a grant from the National Institute for Health Research (NIHR) under its Health Technology Assessment programme

design.quote: Phase 3 open label randomised controlled trial

population.value: UK, aged ≥16 y, not taking vitamin D
population.quote: 6200 people aged ≥16 years who were not taking vitamin D

intervention.value: 800 or 3200 IU/day for 6 months if 25(OH)D <75 nmol/L
intervention.quote: lower dose vitamin D (800 IU/day, n=1550) or higher dose vitamin D (3200 IU/day, n=1550) to those with blood 25(OH)D concentration <75 nmol/L

comparator.value: no offer of testing or supplementation
comparator.quote: compared with no offer of testing or supplementation (n=3100)

effect.value: OR 1.26 (95% CI 0.96–1.66) lower dose; OR 1.09 (0.82–1.46) higher dose
effect.quote: odds ratio 1.26, 95% confidence interval 0.96 to 1.66) and 76/1515 (5.0%) in the higher dose group (1.09, 0.82 to 1.46)

funding.value: Barts Charity, Pharma Nord, DSM Nutritional Products and others
funding.quote: This study was supported by Barts Charity (refs MGU0459 and MGU0466), Pharma Nord, the Fischer Family Foundation, DSM Nutritional Products

design.quote: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
